newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bertrand Faure says may sell Delsey.
newsitem.headline: Bertrand Faure says may sell Delsey.

text.p: French car seat maker Bertrand Faure said on Wednesday it could start looking for a buyer for its luggage manufacturing unit Delsey this year.
"It's not impossible that we will look for a buyer (for Delsey) as of this year," said company chairman Daniel Dewavrin, announcing the company's 1996 results.

The group reported that net attributable profit jumped to 364.4 million francs from 115.8 million, driven by its automotive seating operations whose operating income climbed by 242.4 million francs to reach a total of 662.7 million.
It said it expected a furthe profit increase in 1997.
Faure had already indicated that Delsey did not have a long term future inside the group and that a buyer would be sought after the subsidiary's finances recovered.
Delsey cut its net consolidated loss in 1996 to 34 million francs from 56 millions in 1995. North American losses were reduced to 29 million from 37 million.
Finance director Philippe Douay said that Faure was hoping that Delsey would return to breakeven this year.
"The restructuring plan for Delsey is practically finished with the transfer of production of soft-sided baggage to southeast Asian countries, he said.
